'''The workstation compat layer''' is the seam between the
<code>nexuslbs/deepseek-harness</code> (dsh) runtime and the plugin set loaded
into the workstation service. It was documented and hardened in
2026-09-25 and its adapter was retired the next day.

== Decision (recorded) ==

'''RETIRED - NO SHIM (operator reversal, 2026-09-26).''' The
<code>workstation-http</code> compat adapter was deleted. The plugins are now
proper native dsh plugins with typed tool definitions and the harness credentials
service; workstation is the only implementation, with no workbench support. The
HTTP surface the adapter used to own became a minimal native dsh plugin,
<code>plugins/http-surface</code>.

{{OmniFact
|what=native dsh plugin set plus a minimal http-surface facade
|where=the workstation service and workstation-plugins
|status=retired adapter, native plugins shipped
|source=Projects/Omniagent/Workstation-Compat-Layer.md
}}

== The seam in one paragraph ==

The harness was loaded with the plugin package set, which had been written
against the workbench core cordis API. The harness API differed in exactly two
code-level places, both once closed by the compat layer; everything else
(<code>ctx.effect</code>, service lookup via <code>ctx.get</code> and
<code>ctx.&lt;svc&gt;</code>) was already cordis-native. The harness also shipped
no workbench-core HTTP surface, so the adapter owned the
<code>/health</code> and <code>POST /api/tool/call</code> routes too.

== Contract table ==

{| class="wikitable"
|-
! Contract !! Workbench reference !! dsh !! Verdict
|-
| cordis runtime || cordis 4.0.0-rc.10 || vendored cordis 4.0.4 || compatible - same 4.x lineage
|-
| plugin module shape || manifest plus <code>name</code> / <code>inject</code> / <code>apply(ctx, config)</code> || <code>name</code> / <code>inject</code> / <code>apply(ctx)</code> || compatible entry convention
|-
| tool registration || <code>registerTool({name, handler, parameters, description})</code> || <code>register(defineTool({name, description, parameters, output, execute}))</code> || RETIRED - plugins register natively
|-
| tool-call HTTP body || <code>POST /api/tool/call</code> with <code>{"tool","params"}</code> || no such route in the harness || RETIRED - the native facade owns the same wire contract
|-
| credentials || file backend at a fixed path || <code>$DSH_HOME/.credentials.yaml</code> plus a provider-managed store || RETIRED - plugins resolve through <code>ctx.credentials</code>
|-
| plugin discovery || manifest plus a roster || cordis loader entries via <code>--patch</code> || different, and permitted by the operator
|}

== What the adapter used to bridge ==

# '''Tool registration shim''' - re-installed <code>registerTool</code> as a thin
   adapter that converted the parameter map to JSON Schema, supplied the required
   default output, and forwarded to the real registry.
# '''Credentials file fallback''' - the harness already ships a credentials
   service, so the adapter augmented it instead of shadowing it: a reference the
   harness could not resolve fell back to the operator file, and an unresolved
   reference returned the harness result.
# '''HTTP facade''' - <code>GET /health</code> plus <code>/healthz</code> and
   <code>/api/tools</code>, and <code>POST /api/tool/call</code>, with raw errors
   returned verbatim.

== Native layout (2026-09-26) ==

* <code>workbench-plugins/definitions/tools.ts</code> and
  <code>definitions/credentials.ts</code> own the dsh-native consumer contracts.
* Every tool registers <code>ctx.tools.register(defineTool({...}))</code>;
  <code>plugins/http-surface</code> is the minimal native dsh HTTP surface.
* <code>omni-root/config/workstation.yml</code> is the run-time
  <code>--patch</code> overlay; external-service targets live there, never in
  code or in a plugin repo.
* The workstation image is browser-free, ships no email client and bundles no
  capability plugins; see [[Container Mount Map]] for where the external
  checkouts are mounted.
